Where most of the work happens

IFS-informed EMDR

Standard EMDR asks you to hold a memory and let the processing run. For people with developmental trauma that instruction often meets an internal objection: a part of you that has spent years keeping the material at a distance, and has good reasons. IFS-informed EMDR treats that objection as information rather than resistance. Processing starts when the protective parts agree to it, not when the protocol says it is time. This is the focus of Reem Glasco's clinical work, and the reason most people arrive here. Sessions are 50 minutes at $240 self-pay, online across Texas, with Blue Cross Blue Shield accepted.

Why standard EMDR stalls

If the trauma is a single event and your nervous system is otherwise stable, standard protocol often works well and quickly. If the trauma is developmental, something else is true: parts of you organized around keeping that material away, and they did it for years, competently, because at the time it was the only thing keeping you functional.

Ask those parts to stand aside for a protocol and they will do what they have always done. The processing floods, or it flatlines, or you find yourself unable to bring the target to mind at all. From the outside it looks like EMDR not working. From the inside it is a protector doing its job.

What changes with parts work

Internal Family Systems gives us language for that. Rather than pushing past the protector, we get to know it. What is it afraid will happen if you go near this? What does it need in place first? What has it been carrying, and for how long?

Reem's emphasis is phases one and two, history-taking and preparation, because that is where stalled EMDR actually stalls. Build enough stability and enough internal agreement there, and the later phases stop being a fight.

What this looks like in session

  • Naming the parts in the room: the one that wants to heal, the one that wants to leave, the one that thinks this is self-indulgent.
  • Unblending, so you can look at a part rather than speak as it.
  • Asking permission from protectors before any target gets processed.
  • Resourcing and stabilization that a protective part actually trusts.
  • Slowing or pausing processing when a part objects, and treating that objection as information rather than resistance.

It tends to fit when

  • EMDR has been tried before and went nowhere, or went badly.
  • You flood, dissociate or go blank when you approach the material.
  • Part of you wants this and part of you really does not.
  • The trauma is developmental and layered rather than a single event.

Reem completed steps one through three of IFS-informed EMDR training in 2025, is EMDR certified and an EMDRIA Approved Consultant, and consults with other therapists on exactly this problem.

Questions about IFS-informed EMDR

What is Internal Family Systems?

A model that treats the mind as made up of parts, each with its own job and its own fears, around a core self that is not a part. Protective parts manage pain; exiled parts carry it. The work is relational: you get to know a part rather than overriding it.

Is this the same as full IFS therapy?

No. This is EMDR practiced with IFS awareness, not IFS as a standalone treatment. The parts work is in service of making EMDR usable for developmental trauma, particularly in the preparation phases.

My EMDR flooded me last time. Will that happen again?

It is the specific thing this approach exists to prevent. Flooding usually means processing started before the parts holding the material had agreed to it, or before there was enough resourcing for them to trust. Both are preparation problems, and preparation is where the emphasis sits here.

How is this different from just going slower?

Pace helps, but the obstacle is not usually speed. A protector that believes something catastrophic follows from touching this material will object at any speed. What changes things is finding out what it is protecting and what it needs, which is a different conversation rather than a slower one.

Do I have to believe in parts for this to work?

No. Parts language is a working model, not a metaphysics. Plenty of people use it as a convenient way of describing conflicting impulses they already recognize, and the work proceeds the same either way.
